definitions.explanation: A longer, indirect route taken instead of the most direct path, whether by necessity (road closure) or by choice.

definitions.gloss: roundabout approach; indirect way of doing something
definitions.explanation: A figurative detour — taking a longer or less efficient approach to achieving a goal. Can imply either inefficiency or a valuable learning experience.

examples.japanese: {工事|こうじ}{中|ちゅう}なので{回|まわ}り{道|みち}をした。
examples.english: There was construction, so I took a detour.

examples.japanese: {景色|けしき}のいい{回|まわ}り{道|みち}を{楽|たの}しんだ。
{急|いそ}いでいるのに{回|まわ}り{道|みち}をさせられて{困|こま}った。
examples.english: I was in a hurry and was frustrated at being forced to take a detour.

examples.japanese: {人生|じんせい}に{回|まわ}り{道|みち}はつきものだ。
examples.english: Detours are a natural part of life.

examples.japanese: {回|まわ}り{道|みち}のように{見|み}えても、その{経験|けいけん}はきっと{役|やく}に{立|た}つ。
examples.english: Even if it seems like a detour, that experience will surely prove useful.

examples.japanese: {効率|こうりつ}を{求|もと}めすぎると、かえって{回|まわ}り{道|みち}になることもある。
examples.english: Seeking too much efficiency can actually end up being a roundabout approach.

notes:
USAGE:
{回|まわ}り{道|みち} can be used as a noun or as a suru-verb ({回|まわ}り{道|みち}する — to take a detour). The figurative sense is very common, especially when reflecting on life choices or career paths.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {回|まわ}り{道|みち}をする (take a detour)
- {回|まわ}り{道|みち}になる (turn out to be a detour)
- {人生|じんせい}の{回|まわ}り{道|みち} (life's detours)
- {少|すこ}し{回|まわ}り{道|みち}する (take a slight detour)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{迂回|うかい} means "detour" in a more formal or technical sense, often used for traffic or military contexts. {遠回|とおまわ}り means "going the long way around" and is close in meaning but emphasizes distance.
